records.title: Covered earnings counted up to each year's contribution and benefit base, from 1951
records.purpose: Count each year's earnings in the average only up to that year's taxable maximum, back to 1951, before indexing them.
records.statement: socialSecurity/piaFromEarnings.ts#computePiaFromEarnings caps each year's covered earnings at that year's contribution and benefit base, socialSecurity/ssaWageData.ts#WAGE_BASE_BY_YEAR (SSA's bases for every year from 1937 through 2026, read through #wageBaseForYearOrLatest, which uses the latest published base only for a later year SSA has not set), before wage-indexing them (42 U.S.C. 415(e)(1): "there shall not be counted the excess over $3,600 in the case of any calendar year after 1950 and before 1955", and so on through the section 430 base from 1975). Its window of years starts at 1951 (#FIRST_COMPUTATION_BASE_YEAR, the first of "the calendar years after 1950", 415(b)(2)(B)(ii)) or the year the worker turns 22, whichever is later, and ends with the year before 62; the five lowest indexed years are dropped and the rest averaged over their months, floored to a dollar. Units: nominal USD per year for earnings, per month for the average. Rounding: each indexed year floored to a dollar and the average floored to a dollar.

formula.expression: counted(y) = min(earnings(y), base(y)); indexed(y) = floor(counted(y) x AWI(e - 2) / AWI(y)) for y <= e - 2, else counted(y); years y from max(1951, b + 22) to e - 1; AIME = floor(sum of all but the five lowest indexed / (12 x (count - 5)))

variables.meaning: Covered earnings reported or projected for year y
Contribution and benefit base for year y: SSA's from 1937, the latest published for a later year
National average wage index for year y, the latest published for a later year
Eligibility year, the year the worker turns 62 (effective birth year plus 62)
Effective birth year (a January 1 birth counts in the prior year)

formula.timing: once per earnings history, before the projection
formula.rounding: each indexed year and the average floored to a whole dollar

limits: Each indexed year is floored to a dollar where 20 CFR 404.211(d)(3) rounds to the penny (cfr-20-404-211-d-3-indexed-earnings-nearer-penny), and the window leaves out the age-21 year and years from 62 to first entitlement (usc-42-415-b-2-b-ii-iii-initial-computation-base-window)
Eligibility before 1979 is refused, so the earliest window year is 1951 for a worker born from 1917 to 1929; the transitional guarantee for workers born 1917 to 1921 is not modeled

The old-start computation (20 CFR 404.240 through 404.243), which can count earnings from 1937 through 1950 for a worker born in 1929 or earlier, is not modeled: earnings before 1951 count for nothing here. SSA pays the highest PIA among the methods a worker qualifies for, so leaving it out can only understate the PIA, and only for a worker 97 or older in 2026
A year later than the last published base or wage index uses the latest published figure, and the result says so (usesStandInForFutureTables)
The PIA it yields is in eligibility-year dollars; the projection raises it by the cost-of-living increases since (pia-cost-of-living-since-eligibility)

records.title: Zero years in the averaged earnings
records.purpose: Count how many of the years averaged into a worker's AIME have no earnings.
records.statement: socialSecurity/piaFromEarnings.ts#computePiaFromEarnings publishes zeroYearsInAime, the number of entries of yearsUsedInAime, the indexed amounts it averaged into the AIME, that are 0, beside computationYearCount, the number of those years. Units: years. Rounding: none; integers.

formula.expression: zeroYearsInAime = count of v in yearsUsedInAime with v = 0

variables.meaning: Indexed earnings of the benefit computation years, the largest after the dropout

formula.timing: once per earnings history

limits: Counts the years this computation averaged, so it follows its computation-year window: always 35 years for a worker whose window has 40, the base years from 22 to 61 (usc-42-415-b-2-b-ii-iii-initial-computation-base-window)

records.title: Benefits received per dollar of Social Security tax paid
records.purpose: Compare the benefits a person is paid, on their own record or a former spouse's when larger, with the Social Security tax their career pays, both in today's dollars.
records.statement: socialSecurity/analysis/oasdiReturn.ts#oasdiReturnForPerson takes, for a person with an earnings history and a PIA the projection can pay, the expected present value of their benefits from the start year (socialSecurity/analysis/expectedValue.ts#expectedPvSingle at the stream's claim age with its months, the former-spouse records and the earnings test on the person's wages; a person in a couple is married while the spouse lives, weighted by the spouse's survival), the benefits already received from the claim year to the year before the start at the start-year amount (#singleBenefitInYear for each of those years, with no discount), and the OASDI tax in today's dollars (#oasdiPaidIn): paid in so far, and on the projected work, the years socialSecurity/piaFromEarnings.ts#resolveStreamPiaMonthly's computation fills from the earnings projection, so the tax and the PIA cover the same career; #benefitsToContributionsRatio divides the sum of the first two by the sum of the last two, and gives no ratio when nothing is paid in. A benefit the ledger pays as a disability benefit from its onset (#disabilityReplacesClaimAge) gets no comparison, and the page says why. Units: a pure number. Rounding: none; the page prints two decimals and "x".

formula.expression: ratio = (getBackPv + receivedBeforeStart) / (paidInToday + projectedToday), none when the sum <= 0

variables.meaning: Expected present value of the benefits from the start year
Benefits from the claim year to the year before the start, at the start-year amount
OASDI tax paid so far, in start-year dollars
OASDI tax on the projected work the PIA counts, in start-year dollars

formula.timing: once, at the start year

limits: The tax paid is restated for prices only, with no interest, while the future benefits are discounted at the chosen real rate

The benefits the person is paid on their own record, or on a former spouse's when larger (a divorced spouse's while unmarried: in a single household, or in a couple after the spouse's death); the insurance value of disability and survivor benefits, benefits paid to others on the record and a current spouse's benefit are left out

The benefits from the start year carry the earnings test on the person's wages; the benefits already received are counted as paid in full, since the plan holds no record of what was withheld before it starts
A benefit paid as a disability benefit from its onset is not compared, since the claim age the get-back is priced at would not start it
Benefits already received are counted at the start-year amount, a constant real amount, not as they were paid
The employer's share is shown beside it as context, not counted in the tax paid

records.title: Covered-work credit estimate
records.purpose: Estimate the Social Security credits an earnings history earns, against the 40 a retirement benefit generally needs.
records.statement: socialSecurity/analysis/credits.ts#estimateCredits returns the entered credit count when there is one; otherwise it adds the history's rows by calendar year and sums #creditsForYear: from 1978, min(4, floor(earnings / that year's quarter-of-coverage amount)) with SSA's amounts (socialSecurity/ssaWageData.ts#QUARTER_OF_COVERAGE_AMOUNT_BY_YEAR, $250 in 1978 to $1,890 in 2026, the latest for a later year); before 1978, min(4, floor(earnings / 50)); nothing before 1937; capped at 40 in total. Eligible means at least 40. Units: credits. Rounding: floor for each year.

formula.expression: credits = min(40, sum_y min(4, floor(E(y) / QC(y)))), QC(y) = SSA amount from 1978, 50 before, no credit before 1937

variables.meaning: Covered earnings in year y, the rows for the year added
Earnings that earn one quarter of coverage in year y

formula.timing: once per earnings history

limits: Years before 1978 were credited by calendar quarter with $50 of wages in the quarter, which an annual amount cannot show; the estimate counts the most such a year could earn, one per $50 up to four
The $100 self-employment rule before 1978 is not applied separately
Not an insured-status determination: no quarter assignment, and no disability or survivor rules; the warning invites the user to enter the count
A year after 2026 uses the 2026 amount until SSA publishes its own

records.title: Consumer Price Index annual averages
records.purpose: The yearly consumer price level used to restate past Social Security taxes in today's dollars.
records.statement: socialSecurity/cpiU.ts#CPI_U_ANNUAL_AVERAGE carries the annual average of the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers, U.S. city average, all items, not seasonally adjusted (BLS series CUUR0000SA0, 1982-84 = 100), for each year from 1937 through 2025, #CPI_U_LATEST_YEAR. Units: index points. Rounding: none; one decimal before 2007 and three after, as published.
limits: October 2025 was not collected; the 2025 average is the one published
A year after 2025 has no average, and the paid-in figure uses the plan's inflation from 2025 on

records.title: Delayed retirement credit factor
records.purpose: Credit a percentage of PIA per month after full retirement age, stopping at age 70, at the rate for the date of birth.
records.statement: socialSecurity/benefitFactor.ts#delayedRetirementFactor increases the retirement benefit by r percent of PIA per month after the normal retirement age, capped at the months available through age 70, so there is no credit past 70. Claiming at or before NRA returns a factor of 1. The rate r is the 20 CFR 404.313(b)(2) credit for the effective birth year, from #delayedCreditMonthlyPct: 2/3 of 1 percent for births after January 1, 1943, and from 5/8 down to 1/12 of 1 percent for earlier births; claimFactor and the survivor base pass it, and the function defaults to 2/3. Units: a dimensionless factor on PIA. Rounding: none.

formula.expression: factor = 1 + min(m, max(0, c)) x r / 100, and 1 when m <= 0

variables.meaning: Months claimed after the normal retirement age
Maximum credited months from NRA through age 70
Credit per month for the effective birth year (2/3 for births after January 1, 1943)
variables.domain: a rate from the 20 CFR 404.313(b)(2) table

formula.timing: once per claim

limits: No direct census family: the factor multiplies PIA on the way to the published annual benefit
Delayed credits apply to the worker's own retirement benefit only; spousal benefits earn none
The cap is supplied by the caller as the months from that person's NRA to age 70, so the record claims the credit rate and the cap behaviour, not the NRA schedule

records.title: Own benefit plus the separately reduced spouse excess
records.purpose: Pay a person entitled to both an own benefit and a spouse or divorced-spouse benefit the own benefit plus the reduced excess of half the worker's PIA over the own PIA.
records.statement: socialSecurity/dualEntitlement.ts#spouseDualEntitlementMonthly returns max(own, min(own, ownPia) + max(0, spouseBase - ownPia) x spouseFactor), where own is the claimant's own benefit as paid, ownPia the claimant's PIA and spouseBase one half of the worker's PIA: the own benefit plus the excess reduced by the spouse factor (42 U.S.C. 402(q)(3)(B), 402(k)(3)(A); POMS RS 00615.250), and for an own benefit with delayed credits the larger of that benefit and the combined amount computed without them (POMS RS 00615.694). The spouse factor is the spouse reduction, 25/36 of 1% for each of the first 36 months before full retirement age and 5/12 of 1% beyond, at the claimant's age in the first month of the spouse benefit (402(q)(6)(A)(ii)): #spouseEntitlementAgeMonths takes the later of the claimant's own configured claim and the claimant's age in the month the worker's benefit starts, the worker's configured claim month for a current spouse (the month the claim age is attained, the plan's claim-age convention) or, for a divorced spouse, the first month the ex is 62 throughout (POMS RS 00202.005 B.2.a: "the NH must be 62 throughout the first month of entitlement but need not have filed a claim for benefits"), since with deemed filing (402(r)) the claimant is taken to apply for the spouse benefit as soon as it is available. projection/internal/annualSocialSecurity.ts#annualSocialSecurity uses it for the lower earner of a couple, with half the worker's PIA first held to the room his family maximum leaves above his PIA (familyMaximum.ts#currentSpouseMonthlyUnderFamilyMaximum), socialSecurity/maritalBenefits.ts#maritalBenefitFor for a divorced spouse, and the claim-milestone insight for its prior-year reconstruction. Units: nominal USD per month, in today's dollars before COLA and haircut. Rounding: none.

formula.expression: total = max(own, min(own, ownPia) + max(0, 0.5 x workerPia - ownPia) x f(s)); s = max(ownClaimMonths, workerStartMonth - claimantAgeZeroMonth); f(s) = 1 at s >= FRA, else 1 - (min(36, FRA - s) x 25/36 + max(0, FRA - s - 36) x 5/12) / 100

variables.meaning: Claimant's own old-age benefit as paid, after the claim factor
Claimant's own primary insurance amount; 0 with no own benefit
Worker's (or the ex's) primary insurance amount
Claimant's age in total months in the first month of the spouse benefit, after any earnings-test credit for months the spouse benefit was withheld
Calendar month the worker's record first supports the spouse benefit: the worker's configured claim month, or the first month the ex is 62 throughout
Claimant's full retirement age in total months

formula.timing: once per claimant per projection year

limits: One claim age serves the own and the spouse benefit, and a spouse benefit is paid only from the year both the claimant and the worker have reached their configured claim ages; the months within a year follow the payable-month rule of social-security-payable-months

A divorced spouse's benefit is paid from the calendar year of the first month the ex is 62 throughout, and the ledger pays that whole year, its annual convention for a first year (maritalBenefits.ts#isDivorcedSpouseEligible); an ex born in December after the 2nd starts it the next January, so the year the ex turns 62 pays only the own benefit (worksheet case I)
For people born before January 2, 1954, who could restrict an application to the spouse benefit, the one claim age cannot express that choice; they are priced as if they applied for both

A worker on disability benefits is taken to start at the claim age configured for him, not at the disability onset, and a claimant on disability benefits is priced with the same composition; 42 U.S.C. 402(q)(3)(C) and (D) govern a disabled claimant and are not modeled separately
The family maximum caps a current spouse's excess only; a divorced spouse's benefit is outside the family maximum, and no child benefits are modeled

The spouse reduction is credited with the months of the spouse benefit's own reduction period in which it was subject to an earnings-test deduction, the worker's excess charged to the family or the claimant's own, counted for that record (the current spouse, or that former-spouse entry) from the benefit's first month (poms-rs-00615-482-arf-crediting-months), and the credit takes effect in the claimant's full-retirement-age month (cfr-20-404-412-b-arf-effective-fra-month); the claim-milestone insight reconstructs the prior year from configured claim ages without that credit

A couple member's divorced-spouse benefit on a living ex's record starts no earlier than the January after the current spouse's death, and is reduced for the claimant's age in its first month (usc-42-402-b-1-C-divorced-spouse-after-widowhood)

records.title: Early claim reduction factor
records.purpose: Reduce PIA 5/9 of 1% for the first 36 early months and 5/12 of 1% beyond.
records.statement: socialSecurity/benefitFactor.ts#earlyRetirementFactor computes the retirement-benefit factor for months before the normal retirement age by reducing PIA 5/9 of 1% per month for the first 36 months and 5/12 of 1% for each additional month. Claiming at or after NRA returns a factor of 1. Units: a dimensionless factor on PIA. Rounding: none.

variables.meaning: Months claimed before the normal retirement age

formula.timing: once per claim

limits: No direct census family: the factor multiplies PIA on the way to the published annual benefit
The two-band schedule is the worker retirement schedule; the spousal reduction (25/36 of 1% for the first 36 months) and the widow(er) reduction are different rules

records.title: Retirement/survivor family maximum from PIA
records.purpose: The monthly ceiling every auxiliary benefit on a worker record shares, from that worker's PIA.
records.statement: socialSecurity/familyMaximum.ts#familyMaximumMonthlyFromPia takes a monthly PIA P and an eligibility year, reads that year's three family-maximum bend points b1 < b2 < b3 from FAMILY_MAXIMUM_BEND_POINTS (2026: 1,643, 2,371 and 3,093 dollars per month; a year with no published triplet falls back to the latest one on file), and returns floorToDime(1.50 min(P, b1) + 2.72 min(max(P - b1, 0), b2 - b1) + 1.34 min(max(P - b2, 0), b3 - b2) + 1.75 max(P - b3, 0)). A PIA at or below zero returns 0. Units: nominal USD per month, before COLA and any trust-fund haircut. Rounding: the sum is floored to the next lower dime, Math.floor(x * 10 + 1e-9) / 10, so the published figure is quantized and the unrounded sum is an intermediate only.

formula.expression: MFB = floorToDime(1.50 min(P, b1) + 2.72 min(max(P - b1, 0), b2 - b1) + 1.34 min(max(P - b2, 0), b3 - b2) + 1.75 max(P - b3, 0))

variables.meaning: Worker primary insurance amount
Family-maximum bend points for the eligibility year
Monthly retirement/survivor family maximum

formula.timing: once per worker record, before COLA and haircut
formula.rounding: floored to the next lower dime

limits: The four band rates 150/272/134/175 percent are the retirement and survivor family maximum, not the disability family maximum, which SSA computes differently

The bend points are eligibility-year values (the year the worker attains 62 under familyMaximumEligibilityYearFromDobParts), not the benefit year; an eligibility year the table does not price falls back to the latest published triplet

RetireGolden models no child dependents, so capAuxiliaryForFamilyMaximum gives the whole room above the worker's PIA (not above the benefit the worker is paid; cfr-20-404-404-family-maximum-counts-the-worker-pia) to the single current-spouse auxiliary. Under this retirement and survivor maximum that room holds a spouse's whole original benefit less the dime rounding of the maximum (under 10 cents a month); the disability maximum of a worker on SSDI can leave no room and is not modeled (usc-42-403-a-6-ssdi-family-maximum). The worker's own benefit is never reduced by this ceiling
The dime floor is part of the published contract: the test compares the floored figure exactly and treats the unrounded sum as an intermediate

records.title: Normal retirement age endpoint
records.purpose: Assign births after 1955-1959 ramp the current-law 67-year full retirement age.
records.statement: socialSecurity/nra.ts#fraForBirthYear assigns effective birth years 1960 and later a normal retirement age of 67 years and 0 months under current law, the endpoint of the ramp whose last step is 66 years and 10 months at 1959, and #fraTotalMonths converts that to 804 total month slots as twelve times the completed years plus the extra months. Units: years, months and total month slots. Rounding: none; integers.

formula.expression: fra(y >= 1960) = { years: 67, extraMonths: 0 }; totalMonths = years x 12 + extraMonths

variables.meaning: Effective birth year (a January 1 birth uses the prior calendar year)

formula.timing: once per person

limits: Simplified to the birth year: the month-of-year refinements of the SSA schedule are not modeled, and a January 1 birth is handled by the separate effective-birth-year rule

The survivor (widow(er)) full retirement age is a different schedule, keyed to the year the survivor turns 60, so it runs two birth years behind this one and reaches 67 for survivors born 1962 and later; registered as usc-42-416-l-survivor-fra-age-60-attainment-cohorts
Current law may change; the record pins what the module states today

records.title: Social Security tax paid in, in today's dollars
records.purpose: Sum the Social Security tax paid over an earnings history, and the tax the projected work the benefit estimate counts will pay, at each year's rate and wage base, restated in today's dollars by consumer prices.
records.statement: socialSecurity/analysis/oasdiReturn.ts#oasdiPaidIn adds the history's rows by calendar year, and for each year from 1937 to the start year taxes the year's earnings capped at its contribution and benefit base (socialSecurity/ssaWageData.ts#WAGE_BASE_BY_YEAR, the latest base for a later year) at the year's effective rate (socialSecurity/oasdiTaxRates.ts#OASDI_TAX_RATE_BY_YEAR: the employee's, or the self-employed rate; the 2026 row for a later year), and restates the tax by I(y) = CPI(L)/CPI(y) x (1 + i)^(start year - L) for a year up to L, the latest year with a published CPI-U annual average (socialSecurity/cpiU.ts), and (1 + i)^(start year - y) after it, with i the plan's inflation. An entered year through the start year is paid in so far; the projected work, the years the PIA computation's earnings projection fills (passed by #oasdiReturnForPerson from socialSecurity/piaFromEarnings.ts#computePiaFromEarnings) and any entered year after the start, is taxed the same way and restated from the start year at the latest, a factor of 1 after it, since the PIA computation counts a later year at its face amount on the latest base and wage index. It publishes the person's tax and the employer's on each part, the one paid so far also as paid, and names the years it did not count: before 1937, or self-employed before 1951. Units: start-year dollars and dollars as paid. Rounding: none.

formula.expression: paidInToday = sum over entered y <= start of min(E(y), base(y)) x rate(y) / 100 x I(y); projectedToday = sum over projected y of min(E(y), base(y)) x rate(y) / 100 x I(min(y, start)); I(y) = CPI(L)/CPI(y) x (1 + i)^(start - L) for y <= L, else (1 + i)^(start - y)

variables.meaning: Covered earnings in year y, the rows for the year added
Contribution and benefit base for year y
Effective OASDI rate for year y: the employee's, or the self-employed rate
CPI-U annual average for year y; the latest year published
The plan's yearly inflation

formula.timing: calendar years from 1937 to the start year, and the projected years after it
formula.rounding: none; the page prints whole dollars

limits: Restated for prices only: no interest is credited on the tax paid, while the benefits it is compared with are discounted at a real rate

The self-employed credits of 2.7, 2.3 and 2.0 percent in 1984, 1985 and 1986 to 1989 were allowed against the combined OASDI and HI tax and are not allocated to OASDI by the source, so the self-employed figure for those years is high by at most those credits
The employer exemption of 2010 for certain new hires is employer-specific and not modeled
Years after the latest published CPI-U annual average, and the step from it to the start year, use the plan's inflation
The history is taken as taxed Social Security earnings: for a self-employed year, net earnings from self-employment, with no separate self-employment deduction

The projected work is the PIA computation's: its assumed earnings at their face amount on the latest published base and today's rates, and only the years its window counts, through the year the person turns 61; with an entered PIA there is no projected work

records.title: Social Security tax rates by year
records.purpose: The general Social Security tax rate each payer paid in each year since 1937.
records.statement: socialSecurity/oasdiTaxRates.ts#OASDI_TAX_RATE_BY_YEAR carries, for every year from 1937 through 2026, the employee's, the employer's and the self-employed OASDI tax rate in percent of taxable earnings, from the SSA table of tax rates: the trust-fund rate, except the employee's 5.4 percent in 1984 and 4.2 percent in 2011 and 2012 and the self-employed 10.4 percent in 2011 and 2012, which the table's footnotes give as the effective rates; there is no self-employed rate before 1951. Units: percent. Rounding: none; the published figures.
limits: The self-employed credits of 1984 to 1989, which the source gives against the combined OASDI and HI tax, are not applied
A year after 2026 uses the 2026 rates, current law, until the table is extended

The rates are the general schedule, not every payer's own: for 2010 most employers were exempt from the employer's OASDI share on wages paid to certain qualified individuals hired after February 3, 2010 (the source's footnote c; 26 U.S.C. 3111(d), added by the HIRE Act, Pub. L. 111-147, section 101, and struck out in 2018), which the table does not model, so the 2010 employer rate is 6.2 percent where such wages bore 0. The same footnote's 2011 and 2012 two-point reduction for employees and the self-employed is applied: 4.2 and 10.4 percent

records.title: An earnings-history PIA raised by the cost-of-living increases since eligibility
records.purpose: Bring a PIA computed from an earnings history from its eligibility year to the projection's first year, one published increase at a time.
records.statement: socialSecurity/piaFromEarnings.ts#piaWithCostOfLivingIncreases multiplies the eligibility-year PIA, year by year from the eligibility year e through the year t before the projection's first year, by one plus that year's cost-of-living increase from socialSecurity/ssaWageData.ts#COLA_PCT_BY_YEAR (SSA's series, 1975 through 2025), flooring to the dime after each step as 42 U.S.C. 415(i)(2)(A)(ii) requires ("any amount so increased that is not a multiple of $0.10 shall be decreased to the next lower multiple of $0.10"); 415(i)(2)(A)(iii) raises the PIA of a person eligible in a year with an increase "by the amount of that increase and subsequent applicable increases". A year SSA has not announced uses the plan's COLA assumption (#socialSecurityColaAssumptionPct: the fixed rate, or the inflation rate under matchInflation) and is reported. projection/simulate.ts#simulatePlan applies it to every PIA derived from earnings before the ledger's own COLA factor, which is 1 in the first year. Units: nominal USD per month. Rounding: floor to the dime after each year.

formula.expression: P(e - 1) = eligibility-year PIA; P(y) = floorToDime(P(y - 1) x (1 + c(y) / 100)) for y = e to t; result P(t), with t = startYear - 1

variables.meaning: Eligibility year, the year the worker turns 62
The year before the projection's first year
variables.domain: integer; no step when t < e

variables.meaning: Cost-of-living increase effective in year y: SSA's published figure, or the plan's COLA assumption for a year not yet announced

formula.timing: once per earnings-history stream, before the projection
formula.rounding: floor to the next lower ten cents after each year

limits: An entered PIA is taken to be in the first year's dollars already, as a PIA shown on a current SSA statement is

A year between the last announced increase and the projection's first year uses the plan's COLA assumption, a stand-in the projection warns about; the ledger's COLA from the first year on is social-security-cola-factor

The projection, the claim-milestone insight and the planner's Social Security pages read the start-year PIA through socialSecurity/piaFromEarnings.ts#resolveStreamPiaMonthly (social-security-pia-resolution); the planner's AIME explainer shows the eligibility-year computation

COLA_PCT_BY_YEAR ends with the increase effective December 2025. From 2027-01-01 the planner's first year is 2027, so every earnings-history PIA past eligibility takes the plan's COLA assumption for the December 2026 increase, with the projection's warning, until SSA's 2026 increase, announced in October 2026, is added to the table with the yearly parameter refresh
The PIA is not recomputed for later earnings (usc-42-415-f-2-post-entitlement-pia-recomputation)

records.title: PIA from AIME across the bend points
records.purpose: Apply 90/32/15 percent across the eligibility-year bend points and floor to a dime.
records.statement: socialSecurity/piaFromEarnings.ts#piaMonthlyFromAime computes monthly PIA from AIME by applying 90% through the first eligibility-year bend point, 32% between the two bend points and 15% above the second, then rounding the result DOWN to the next lower ten cents. The 2026 bend points come from socialSecurity/ssaWageData.ts#PIA_BEND_POINTS, not from the tax parameters. Units: nominal USD per month. Rounding: floor to a dime.

formula.expression: pia = floorToDime(0.90 x min(A, b1) + 0.32 x max(0, min(A, b2) - b1) + 0.15 x max(0, A - b2))

variables.meaning: Average indexed monthly earnings
First bend point for the eligibility year
Second bend point for the eligibility year

formula.timing: once per eligibility year
formula.rounding: floor to the next lower ten cents

limits: The rounding is a floor, not a round-to-nearest; the worksheet's cross-both case happens not to distinguish them, so the evidence carries a separate discriminator that does
Bend points live in the SSA wage data, not in year2026: reading them from the tax parameters finds nothing
An eligibility year past the last published table falls back to the latest published bend points

records.title: Annual household Social Security benefit
records.purpose: The Social Security cash the household is paid in one projection year, after the earnings test.
records.statement: YearResult.incomes.socialSecurity is the sum over living people of that person's benefit for the year, priced by socialSecurity/householdYear.ts#socialSecurityYear, which projection/internal/annualSocialSecurity.ts#annualSocialSecurity calls and the Social Security analysis models share. The year is composed month by month where a month can differ from the one before: a stream's first paying month (12 - claim months in the claim year, all 12 after), the months both spouses are paid, and each full-retirement-age and survivor-full-retirement-age month. In each month each own retirement stream is PIA x the claim-age factor; a divorced-spouse, current-spouse spousal (the claimant's own monthly PLUS the reduced excess of half the higher PIA over the claimant's own PIA, the dual-entitlement-composition record; for a current spouse half the higher PIA is first held to the family maximum less that PIA) or survivor candidate REPLACES the running amount when it is larger, rather than adding to it; the month's amounts are times the COLA factor and the haircut. A year with no such boundary is priced as one product per stream, monthly x payable months x COLA x haircut. The earnings test then charges each working person's excess earnings month by month from January, only to months the person is paid and that fall before the person's full-retirement-age month: half the wages above the lower exempt amount before the calendar year of that month, and in it a third of the wages of the months before that month above the higher amount, reduced to the next lower dollar. A worker's excess is charged first against the family benefit on his record, his benefits and the spouse benefit on his record, the rest of a partial month shared two to one; each other person's excess is then charged against what is left of that person's benefits. Each month of a benefit's reduction period with a deduction is a crediting month, and it raises that benefit from its full-retirement-age month (the survivor full-retirement-age month for a widow(er) benefit). Units: nominal dollars per year. Rounding: the excess earnings are reduced to the dollar; benefits and the partial-month shares are not rounded.

formula.expression: benefit = sum over living people and months of max(own, marital candidate) x cola x haircut, less the months' deductions; excess = floor((wages - lower) / 2) before the FRA year, floor((wages x b / 12 - higher) / 3) in it, charged month by month from January to months before the FRA month

Months of the FRA year before the FRA month

formula.rounding: the excess earnings are reduced to the next lower dollar; benefits are not rounded

limits: The own-claim-year case is constructible exactly as the worksheet now states it: a 1960 birth has FRA 67y0m, so a 64y3m claim is 33 months early and the factor is 1 - 33 x (5/9 of 1%) = 49/60, while the claim-age month of 3 pays 12 - 3 = 9 months in the claim year. The first derivation instead paired a 0.8 factor with those nine months (0.8 is exactly 36 months before FRA, whose claim-age month is 0 and which therefore pays all 12), and that was corrected on 2026-09-18; the incompatible pair is now the worksheet's first wrong reading, asserted as not matching

Beyond the worksheet's inputs the evidence plans fix, for the claim-year and later-year cases: a 1960-born single filer claiming at 64y3m on one plan whose projection starts in 2024, the year that birth attains 64, so the claim year is the first projection year and its COLA factor is exactly 1; zero inflation and zero return; a fixed 6%/year ssCola so the second projection year's factor is exactly 1.06; ssHaircut cutPct 5 from the start year; and a cash account to fund the year

The two-person case asserts the REPLACEMENT rule, so both people claim at their own FRA (claim and spousal factors 1) in the projection's first year, where the COLA factor is 1 and no haircut applies; the family maximum is left non-binding by the PIAs chosen

The earnings-test case is a separate 1962-born plan claiming at 64y0m, where the 0.8 factor and 12 payable months ARE the compatible pair, and is asserted in 2026 so the published parameters’ $24,480 below-FRA limit is unindexed; the wage row that drives it is ordinary income and is taxed, which does not enter this family

The family-charge cases (E5 and E7b) are a couple born in January 1964, both claiming at 62 in 2026 with no inflation, so every month of 2026 is in both reduction periods and the family maximum does not bind

The published field is the PAID benefit; the amount withheld is a separate field (ssEarningsTestWithheld), and the months withheld raise the benefit from its full-retirement-age month rather than being lost

Rounding: the excess earnings are reduced to the next lower dollar (42 U.S.C. 403(f)(3)); benefits and the partial-month shares are not rounded, where 20 CFR 404.304(f) reduces each monthly benefit, after all deductions, to the next lower multiple of $1, so a month can be up to a dollar above what SSA pays

Wages are the plan's wage rows, whole calendar years spread evenly over their months: there is no grace year and no non-service month (cfr-20-404-435-grace-year-monthly-earnings-test), only wage streams are earnings (usc-42-403-f-5-earnings-counted), and after the latest published year the exempt amounts grow at the plan's inflation (usc-42-403-f-8-earnings-test-exempt-amounts)

A claim at a whole age pays the whole calendar year it is attained (social-security-payable-months); the months before the claim month are paid and can be charged, but are not in the reduction period and are not credited

A worker's excess is charged against a household member's spouse benefit on his record; a former spouse's record carries no plan earnings, and a disability beneficiary is tested against substantial gainful activity instead of the earnings test

Restated 2026-09-27 (decision D-SS-LAW-2): the current-spouse candidate adds to the claimant’s own monthly benefit, held at the own PIA, the excess of half the higher PIA over the claimant’s own PIA reduced by the spousal factor (dual-entitlement-composition). Restated 2026-09-29 (decision D-SS-ANALYSIS-EARNINGS-TEST): the year is composed month by month where a month can differ, and the earnings test is charged month by month with the family charge, the FRA-year months, the dollar floor, reduction-period crediting and the adjustment from the FRA month, where it was one annual amount with rounded months and the adjustment from January. Neither restatement is reviewed yet

No discrepancy remains in the two-person case: the year function builds the current-spouse candidate as the claimant's own monthly benefit PLUS the capped spousal excess ($300 + $700 = $1,000) and replaces the running amount with that total, which is what a dually-entitled spouse is actually paid, so the household is $36,000 and the worksheet expects $36,000. The first derivation read the ledger comment's "replaces the running amount" as replacing the own benefit with the excess alone and expected $32,400; it was corrected on 2026-09-18, and $32,400 is now the worksheet's second wrong reading, asserted as not matching

records.title: Claim-age refinement to the month
records.purpose: Refine the sweep's whole-year winner to the month on the same objective, and publish its signed changes against the winner.
records.statement: decisions/claimAgeSweep.ts#refineClaimAgeMonthly prices, through #refineClaimMonths, for each open claim in the canonical people order (model/peopleOrder.ts, never list order), every claim from a year below the winner's age to a year above it (62 to 70, none below the age reached in the start year; months 0 to 11, and only 70y0m at 70), with the other claims at the running best, in whole passes repeated until one changes no claim, the windows staying around the starting whole years, and a combination priced once not priced again (decision D-PEOPLE-ORDER, rule R7); there is no pass cap, since a changing pass takes a strictly greater primary metric and a combination's row is fixed once priced, so no combination is the incumbent twice and the search always ends at a fixed point, within one more pass than the windows hold combinations, a bound kept only as a guard that throws, and #refineClaimMonths reports the passes it ran (round-one review of #765, issue 4), each month through decisions/evaluateCandidate.ts#evaluateCandidate against the plan as entered and ranked alone by the sweep's objective policy (decisions/tournament.ts#rankEvaluations, margin 0). A month replaces the incumbent only when its row is eligible under the objective's constraints and its primary metric is strictly greater; a greater but ineligible month is counted and rejected. It publishes estateChangeVsWinner, the refined ending after-tax estate minus the winner's, and primaryChangeVsWinner, the objective's own difference, both signed and unrounded. Units: nominal dollars of the plan's last year, and the objective's own units. Rounding: none.

formula.expression: take month m over incumbent i  <=>  eligible(m) and primary(m) > primary(i); estateChangeVsWinner = estate(refined) - estate(winner); primaryChangeVsWinner = primary(refined) - primary(winner)

variables.meaning: The objective policy's metric of month m against the plan as entered
Month m meets every hard constraint of the policy (money-lasts, the estate floor, a structural diagnostic)
Ending after-tax estate of the plan with month m's claim
variables.unit: nominal USD of the plan's last year

formula.timing: one full ledger run per combination tried: up to 36 per claim per pass (the months from a year below the whole-year pick to a year above it: 36, or 24 for a pick of 62, 25 for 69 and 13 for 70, fewer when the age reached in the start year cuts the window), 13 to 72 in the first pass, and a later pass prices only the combinations not yet priced

limits: Coordinate passes to a fixed point within a year of the whole-year winner: a month further away, or a combination that needs both claims moved at once, is not tried, and the page says "no month within a year of the whole-year pick ranks higher" rather than "optimal"

Bridge durability and survivor liquidity score a month that removes the bridge or survivor years on the estate change, as the sweep does, until the objective-policy change ranks them on one fixed window
Runs on request, 0.2 to 0.6 seconds on the example couples

records.title: Whole-plan Social Security claim-age sweep
records.purpose: Rank every whole-year claim age of the plan's open claims on the full ledger by a chosen objective, and publish the winner's signed estate change against the plan as entered.
records.statement: decisions/claimAgeSweep.ts#sweepClaimAges takes the plan's open claims (socialSecurity/openClaims.ts#openClaims: of the first two Social Security streams with a positive entered PIA or an earnings history, those whose claim year, the birth year plus the claim age's whole years, is not before the start year; the others are already made and keep their own claim age in every row, #isClaimAlreadyMade, social-security-claim-already-made), holds an open claim that is paid as a disability benefit from its onset as the ledger pays it (decisions/generators.ts#claimAgeGridClaims), prices every combination of whole-year ages of the other open claims from #gridClaimAges (62 to 70, none below the age reached in the start year; decisions/generators.ts#socialSecurityClaimGridGenerator) with decisions/evaluateCandidate.ts#evaluateCandidate against the plan as entered, and ranks the rows with decisions/tournament.ts#rankEvaluations under the chosen objective policy with a margin of 0. The verdict (#claimAgeSweepVerdict) is empty with no claim, already-claimed when every claim is already made, disability when every open claim is paid as a disability benefit from its onset (those claims are published as disabilityPersonIds, and held in a ranked sweep), winner when an eligible row strictly improves the objective, otherwise aca-unpriced when no row is eligible and the plan as entered has a year whose premium tax credit cannot be priced (#unpricedAcaYears: each such year with its blocking support codes), ineligible when no row is eligible, flat when two or more eligible rows lie within 0.5 of the first and current-best otherwise. It publishes winnerEstateChangeVsCurrent, the winner's ending after-tax estate minus the plan as entered's (claim months included), signed and unrounded, each row's change the same way, a row as current only when every open claim is a whole year equal to it, and per row whether the objective ranked it on its own metric (objective) or on the estate fallback, because the plan as entered has no survivor or bridge years (estate-fallback-plan, then every row) or because this row has none (estate-fallback-row) (decisions/objectives.ts#rankedMetricBasis). Units: nominal dollars of the plan's last year, published as estateYear. Rounding: none.

formula.expression: change(row) = estate(row) - estate(plan as entered); winner = the first eligible ranked row whose primary metric is above 0; verdict = claimAgeSweepVerdict(ranked, winner exists, unpriced credit years)

variables.meaning: Ending after-tax estate of the plan with the row's whole-year claim ages
variables.unit: nominal USD of the plan's last year

variables.meaning: Ending after-tax estate of the plan with its own claims, months included (the decision context's baseline run)
variables.unit: nominal USD of the plan's last year

variables.meaning: The objective policy's metric against the plan as entered, higher is better
Birth year plus the claim age's whole years; before the start year means already made

formula.timing: one full ledger run per grid row, from the start year
formula.rounding: none; the page prints the sign of the printed magnitude, so a change that prints as $0 has neither

limits: The plan's own conversion strategy is held fixed: a bracket fill resizes to each claim age, a fixed schedule does not. The Optimize page's co-optimization re-optimizes conversions but tries only 62, full retirement age and 70, one stream at a time, on the estate with a 1,000-dollar margin (claim-age-co-optimization), so the two searches can pick different ages, and a gain found here is measured with the plan's own conversions
Whole years only, and at most two streams

A claim counts as already made when its claim year is before the start year, the ledger's annual convention: the ledger ignores the birth month, so a claim in the start year whose month has passed is still treated as open; and a claim at or after full retirement age that was never filed can be paid up to six months back (20 CFR 404.621(a)(2)), which the test treats as made, the conservative side

Withdrawing an application within 12 months of the first month of entitlement, repaying every benefit (20 CFR 404.640(b)(3), (b)(4)), and voluntary suspension from full retirement age (42 U.S.C. 402(z)) are not modeled

Where the premium tax credit cannot be priced in a year of the plan as entered, no row is ranked: a claim age moves the income the credit depends on (26 U.S.C. 36B(d)(2)(B)(iii)); ranking only the rows that leave that income unchanged was measured and is not safe in either direction (an equal stand-in credit changed three of eleven such winners on the example plans)

Bridge durability and survivor liquidity rank a row on the estate change when that row or the plan has no bridge or survivor years, within one ranking; each row says which of the two lacked them, and ranking both on one fixed window in today's dollars is a separate objective-policy change

A disability benefit from its onset has no claim age to sweep: the sweep holds it as the ledger pays it and ranks the other claim, and refuses only when every open claim is one. The benefits-only ranking prices a couple's claims as pairs of claim ages and cannot place a disability benefit on that grid, so it ranks no claim age for either person

records.title: Social Security claim already made
records.purpose: Decide, for every claim-age search, whether a claim was already made before the plan starts, so it is held rather than re-made.
records.statement: socialSecurity/openClaims.ts#isClaimAlreadyMade says a claim at a claim age is already made when its claim year (#claimYearOf: the calendar year of the date of birth plus the claim age's whole years, the months ignored) is before the plan's start year, and open otherwise, the ledger's annual convention. It is the one test every claim-age search applies: #openClaims for the Social Security page's sweep and its month refinement, socialSecurity/analysis/expectedValue.ts#benefitsOnlyRanking, decisions/generators.ts#socialSecurityClaimGenerator for a stream and for each canonical age, projection/optimizePlan.ts#optimizePlanCoOptimizingClaimAge, and the Scenarios page's claim-age lever. A claim already made is held at its own claim age; a claim age whose claim year is before the start year is not offered. Units: calendar years. Rounding: none.

formula.expression: claimYear = birthYear + claimAge.years; alreadyMade = claimYear < startYear

variables.meaning: The calendar year of the person's date of birth as entered (no birth-month or January-1 adjustment)
The whole years of the stream's claim age; its months are ignored
The plan's first projection year

A claim at or after full retirement age that was never filed can still be paid up to six months back (20 CFR 404.621(a)(2)); a claim year before the start year cannot be known to fall within those six months, so the test treats it as made, the conservative side

Withdrawing an application within 12 months of the first month of entitlement, repaying every benefit (20 CFR 404.640(b)(3), (b)(4); a withdrawn application is treated as never filed, 404.640(d)), is not modeled: a claim made stays made
Voluntary suspension from full retirement age to 70 (42 U.S.C. 402(z)) is not modeled, so a claim made cannot earn delayed credits here

records.title: Claiming break-even ages and cumulative benefits
records.purpose: Chart one person's cumulative own benefit at a few claim ages in the plan's dollars, and the age each later claim catches up.
records.statement: socialSecurity/analysis/breakEven.ts#claimBreakEven accumulates, for each compared whole-year claim age c and each age a from 62 through the chart's last age, in calendar year y = birth year + a, the own benefit the ledger's year function (socialSecurity/householdYear.ts#socialSecurityYear) pays the person in y with the claim at c years and 0 months and nothing else on the record: 0 before c, otherwise the start-year PIA x the claim factor for c years and 0 months x 12 x socialSecurity/colaFactor.ts#socialSecurityColaFactor for y x #socialSecurityHaircutFactor for y, the two factors projection/simulate.ts#simulatePlan multiplies every benefit by, less what the earnings test withholds from it on the person's own wages (the plan's wage rows, analysis/expectedValue.ts#personWagesInYear), and from the full-retirement-age month at the claim age raised by the crediting months; it also names the claim ages at which the test withholds. The running total is B_c(a) = B_c(a - 1) x (1 + g) + benefit_c(a) at the chosen return g. For each pair of claim ages e < l it walks the ages at which B_e is positive and reports the first age a with D(a) = B_l(a) - B_e(a) >= 0, at a - 1 + (-D(a - 1)) / (D(a) - D(a - 1)) when the previous difference was negative, else at a; none when no age by the chart's end. #breakEvenClaimAges gives the page's comparison: 62, the full-retirement-age year and 70, each no earlier than the age reached in the start year; a claim age before it is refused. Units: nominal dollars of each year, ages in years. Rounding: none; the page prints the crossing to a tenth of a year and the dollars to whole dollars.

formula.expression: B_c(a) = B_c(a - 1)(1 + g) + [a >= c] x (PIA x f_c(y) x 12 x cola(y) x cut(y) - withheld_c(y)); crossing(e, l) = a - 1 + (-D(a - 1))/(D(a) - D(a - 1)), D = B_l - B_e

variables.meaning: The monthly PIA the projection pays from in its first year
Claim factor for a claim at c years and 0 months, from the full-retirement-age month with the crediting months added (a year's months priced apart when that month falls in it)
What the earnings test withholds from the own benefit in year y on the person's own wages
The projection's cost-of-living factor (1 in its first year) and trust-fund haircut for year y
Yearly return on benefits already received
Whole-year claim ages

formula.timing: annual, a whole year of benefits in the claim-age year
formula.rounding: none; the page rounds for display

limits: The person's own retirement benefit only: no spouse, survivor or divorced-spouse benefit, no taxes, and no mortality, since every charted age is taken as reached

The earnings test on the person's own wages is charged against the own benefit alone, as if nothing else were paid on the record: for a couple's worker whose wages also reach a spouse benefit on his record this withholds more from his own benefit than the family charge would
Wages are the plan's wage rows, whole calendar years spread evenly over their months, with no grace year; only wage streams are earnings (usc-42-403-f-5-earnings-counted)
Whole-year claim ages, paid for the whole claim-age year, as the ledger pays a claim at a whole age

records.title: Social Security COLA factor
records.purpose: Compound the benefit escalator from the projection start, with no escalation in the first year.
records.statement: projection/internal/annualSocialSecurity.ts#annualSocialSecurity receives an ssColaFactor that compounds from the projection start, with factor 1 in the first year, using either the plan's general inflation rate or its fixed ssCola rate, and an ssHaircutFactor. projection/simulate.ts#simulatePlan builds both with socialSecurity/colaFactor.ts#socialSecurityColaFactor, to which it passes its own inflation factor (a Monte Carlo path's when one is supplied), and #socialSecurityHaircutFactor (1 - cutPct / 100 from the haircut year, else 1); the break-even chart and the benefits-only expected value call the same two functions on the plan's deterministic inflation. For a fixed rate the factor at year offset n is (1 + rate)^n, so the published benefit of a stream already in force scales by exactly that factor against its start-year amount. Units: a dimensionless factor. Rounding: none.

formula.expression: ssColaFactor(y) = (1 + ssCola.annualPct / 100)^(y - startYear) for the fixed mode, or the plan inflation factor from startYear to y for matchInflation

variables.meaning: Projection year
First projection year
Plan fixed COLA rate

formula.timing: once per projection year

limits: Asserted at the plan level the comments state rather than by reading a private local: the evidence runs a real projection of a single stream already in force, with twelve payable months and no haircut and no earnings test, so the year's published benefit over the start year's IS the factor the phase received
The two modes are alternatives, never combined: a plan on matchInflation does not additionally apply the fixed rate
The worksheet's 2.8% is year2026.socialSecurity.colaPct used as the plan's fixed rate; the parameter figure is not itself the plan default

records.title: Benefits-only expected present value of Social Security
records.purpose: Value a claiming strategy by its benefits alone: each year's benefits, priced by the ledger's rules, weighted by the chance of being alive and discounted.
records.statement: socialSecurity/analysis/expectedValue.ts values a claiming strategy as the survival-weighted, discounted sum of the benefits on each path the household can take, each year of each path priced by the ledger's own year function (socialSecurity/householdYear.ts#socialSecurityYear, through analysis/householdPaths.ts#priceHouseholdPaths) with the plan's wages and exempt amounts, so the earnings test, the crediting months and the former-spouse records are the ledger's. #expectedPvSingle sums, for each year t from the start year while the person is at most 119, S(t) x paid(t) x (1 + r)^-t, where S is montecarlo/survival.ts#survivalCurve from the current age and paid(t) the year's benefits in start-year dollars (nominal over the plan's inflation factor, which carries the ledger's COLA factor over its inflation factor times the haircut); a claimant in a couple is married while the given spouse lives and unmarried after the spouse's death, weighted by the spouse's survival. #expectedPvCouple sums, for independent lives, S_A(t) S_B(t) both(t) plus, for each earlier death year k of one spouse, the survivor's S(t) x the other's probability of dying in year k x alone(t, k): both(t) is the year on the path on which both are alive, from the start year with no crediting months, and alone(t, k) the survivor's year on the path on which the other died in December of year k, from the crediting months both had reached at the end of year k, the deceased's included. A path stops changing once every claim, full-retirement-age and former-spouse gate is past, and from then its benefits are priced once in today's dollars and carried by the real COLA drift and haircut. #benefitsOnlyRanking prices every whole-year claim-age combination from 62 to 70 (none before the age reached in the start year; 70 alone past it) for one or two claimants on the PIA the projection pays from, and ranks them highest first, on the plan's own household (a lone claimant in a couple is weighted by the spouse's survival), and names for each row the people whose excess earnings the test charges on the path on which everyone lives; the paths do not depend on the rate, so #priceBenefitsOnlyRanking prices them for a plan and start year and #weighBenefitsOnlyRanking weighs them at a rate, and #benefitsOnlyRanking does both on each call and keeps nothing between calls. A claim already made (its claim year, birth year plus claim years, before the start year: socialSecurity/openClaims.ts#isClaimAlreadyMade, the claim-age searches' one test) is held at its own claim age and named, and nothing is ranked when every claim is; a claimant whose benefit is paid as a disability benefit from its onset is named instead. Units: start-year dollars. Rounding: none in the model; the earnings test's excess is reduced to the dollar and benefits are not rounded, as in the ledger.

formula.expression: single: sum_t S(t) paid(t) (1 + r)^-t; couple: sum_t (1 + r)^-t [S_A S_B both(t) + sum_{k<t} S_A(t) D_B(k) alone_A(t, k) + sum_{k<t} S_B(t) D_A(k) alone_B(t, k)]

variables.meaning: Probability of being alive t years after the start year, from the engine's survival curve
Probability of dying in year k, alive through it
A path's benefits in year t after the earnings test, in start-year dollars: nominal over the inflation factor, so the COLA drift and haircut are in them
Real discount rate

formula.timing: annual survival weights, from the start year to age 119; each year priced month by month where a month can differ
formula.rounding: none; the earnings test's excess is reduced to the dollar and benefits are not rounded, as in the ledger

limits: Independent lifetimes on the SSA period table applied to the cohort

A person whose sex is 'average' has the 50/50 mixture of the two sexes' survival curves (survival-probability-product), so a single's value is exactly the mean of a man's and a woman's; a couple of two 'average' people is the average over the four equally likely sex pairings, not "an opposite-sex couple, order unknown", which would differ by up to 0.135 percent of a row on the examples' two such couples and change no top claim age at 0, 2 or 4 percent
Annual steps: a whole year of benefits in each year the survival weight reaches, and deaths in December of the death year, the ledger's convention

One claim age per person: a widow(er) is paid from the later of the year after the death and their own claim year, and cannot take the widow(er) benefit first and their own later, as in the ledger (usc-42-402-r-survivor-deemed-filing-exemption); the survivor switching analysis covers a widow(er) living alone

The earnings test is the ledger's, on the plan's wage rows: whole calendar years spread evenly over their months, with no grace year (cfr-20-404-435-grace-year-monthly-earnings-test); only wage streams are earnings (usc-42-403-f-5-earnings-counted); exempt amounts after the latest published year grow at the plan's inflation (usc-42-403-f-8-earnings-test-exempt-amounts)
Deterministic: the plan's flat inflation carries the wages, the exempt amounts and the COLA; Monte Carlo market paths are not priced here

A claim at a whole age pays the whole calendar year it is attained; its months before the first month of entitlement are paid in full and never charged, so never credited, since no excess is charged to a month for which the person is not entitled (42 U.S.C. 403(f)(1)(A); usc-42-403-f-1-earnings-test-month-charging, poms-rs-00615-482-arf-crediting-months)
No taxes, disability benefit, child benefit or lump-sum death payment

The family maximum is applied with the ledger's own helper (socialSecurity/familyMaximum.ts#currentSpouseMonthlyUnderFamilyMaximum): half the worker's PIA is held first to the maximum less that PIA (20 CFR 404.404), which is at least half the PIA less the rounding of the maximum to the dime, so with one spouse it binds by at most 10 cents a month
A death before 62 passes on the PIA as entered, as the survivor benefit calculation does

A couple member's former-spouse records are priced as the ledger prices them: a survivor record while married only after a remarriage at 60 or later, or with the remarriage age blank, which is read as no remarriage (cfr-20-404-335-ordinary-widow-eligibility); a remarriage before 60 is read as the current marriage and bars the benefit until the January after the current spouse's death; a living ex's record pays from that January (usc-42-402-b-1-C-divorced-spouse-after-widowhood); the plan holds no divorce date, so a divorce of two years or more is taken
Months withheld before the start year, for a claim already made, are not in the plan: every path starts with no crediting months
Benefits are scheduled in full unless the plan sets a haircut, and are worth their start-year amount in real terms unless the plan's COLA differs from its inflation
A claim already made is not re-ranked: withdrawal of an application within 12 months and voluntary suspension from full retirement age are not modeled, as in the claim-age sweep
